name: Raul Gallego Abellán
story_summary: International Emmy Award-winning documentary journalist and filmmaker who co-authored a peer-reviewed study in Frontiers in Communication (November 2024) about immersive documentary journalism. The documentary scene for the research was captured using an Insta360 Pro camera to create a 360° VR scene about undocumented young migrants arriving in Spain. The study tested whether 360° VR documentary generates more empathy in viewers than 2D video on migration issues. Gallego Abellán's documentary series 'Point of No Return' for TV3/3Cat won the International Emmy Award for Best Short-Form Series in 2024. He is founder of Kobukson Media and has worked with the Associated Press, Channel 4 News UK, Al Jazeera, and The Intercept.
why_it_matters: An International Emmy Award-winning journalist used the Insta360 Pro as a tool for social justice documentary journalism — the VR footage he created was scientifically proven to generate greater empathy than 2D on the topic of undocumented migration. This is an entirely new domain for Insta360 creator stories: serious documentary journalism at the highest professional level.
source_quote: The scene was captured with an Insta360 Pro camera, which supports video resolution up to 7,680 × 3,840 with six fisheye lenses.
source_type: peer-reviewed academic journal (Frontiers in Communication, Volume 9, November 26, 2024)

name: Dr. Danielle Millea
story_summary: Senior Learning Officer and filmmaker at the Northern Film School, Leeds Beckett University (now Learning Technologist at University of Leeds), who created filmschool360.com — a free online filmmaking education platform — using Insta360 Pro and Insta360 One X cameras. Over years of research, she filmed 360° video content of filmmaking classes, workshops, and film sets to build a free, accessible learning resource for students who cannot access traditional film schools due to cost, location, or disability. The Insta360 One X proved best for the project. Research published as a PhD thesis and in Interactive Learning Environments (2024), showing 360° video is an effective self-guided learning tool for filmmakers.
product_used: Insta360 Pro and Insta360 One X
why_it_matters: A filmmaker-educator used Insta360 cameras to build a free global filmmaking school accessible to anyone with an internet connection — democratizing film education for students excluded by cost, geography, or disability. Unique application of Insta360: not filming the world, but teaching people how to film it.
source_quote: The Insta360 One X proved best for the study, with twice the storage and batteries compared to other options, and the reduction in resolution was worth the ability to capture more footage with less disruption.
source_type: peer-reviewed academic journal (Interactive Learning Environments, Volume 32, Issue 10, 2024) and ERIC EJ1455920

name: Daniel Dubinski
story_summary: Senior physician and researcher at the Department of Neurosurgery, University Medicine Rostock, who led a team that used an Insta360 Pro 2 camera to create a 360° VR tour of the neurosurgical operating theatre for medical students. The tour covered the route from the hospital entrance through changing rooms, preparation room, and into the neurosurgical operating room. In a randomized study of 24 medical students, those who received VR training showed significantly reduced error rates, faster navigation to the OR, and better gowning compliance during their first operating theatre visit. Published in World Neurosurgery (Epub December 2024, print February 2025).
why_it_matters: A German neurosurgeon used a consumer Insta360 Pro 2 to measurably reduce medical student errors on their first operating theatre visit — a specific, practical clinical education problem solved with a 360° camera. NOTE: Conceptually similar to the existing Tatsuya Tanaka story (Japan neurosurgery VR); human reviewer should assess added value.
source_quote: The VR tour was recorded from a first-person perspective with a static 360° camera (Insta360 Pro 2, Arashi Vision Inc., Berlin, Germany) mounted on a tripod.
source_type: peer-reviewed academic journal (World Neurosurgery, Epub December 19, 2024, print February 2025)
